At the point I'm writing this Killing Floor 2 seems to be just a graphics update with hardly any new features. However, I'm trusting the developers to give us more content as time goes on to make it as good if not better than the previous game.

It's a fun game. It does start to get old eventually, and I wish more players played at the highest difficulty. I also wish the devs would pay a bit more attention to the veteran players. There are loot boxes, but luckily they're all cosmetic items only, you can get some of those type of items for free through gameplay.

Game play overall is fun, strategy and tactics are important, overall would still recommend.

"We see Early Access as an opportunity to involve you, the community, and actually incorporate your feedback as we balance and put the finishing touches on the game. For example, we know how to nail the feel of Killing Floor 2’s weapons, but perfect gameplay balance can only come from large scale play testing. "

This is an outright lie. Tripwire has made 4 major updates now and incorporated absolutely none of the player feedback - changes have only been made when they happen to agree with the player feedback. They continue to release new systems nobody asked for and change the 'vision' of the game seemingly at random (first by including a Versus mode nobody asked for, and then including an opaque and unnecessary resistance system), without regard for playability or fun.

Avoid. Even if you like it today, there's no guarantee it will remain fundamentally the same game next month. Do not buy this game until Tripwire figures out what kind of game they want it to be. Then you can make the decision on whether or not it's a game you like.

They released a crate and key cash shop, like CS:GO, and are talking about adding a versus mode, like L4D, before even finishing all the classes and maps.

It definitely improves on the gameplay of the first game, with the rigid feel of the original's replaced with a more fluid and polished experience, and a fresh coat of graphics to boot.
Sadly, while they added some neat new guns such as the Railgun and Microwave Gun, they also cut out stuff like the M32, ZED Gun, and Husk Launcher, and the lack of any truly new regular enemies is a bit of a disappointment.

I've heard the competetive mode has some balance issues but I never touched it tbh.

While it's certainly not bad by any stretch, I have to wonder why they felt the need to make a sequel if really all they planned to do was tighten up the controls and graphics a bit, and it certainly gives an air of worry that they may have rushed it out of Early Access before fully fleshing it out to push for console releases when it really could've used some more time in the oven.

Still a nice game, though a far cry from a proper sequel.

Good:
* Fun game!
* Lots of classes (known as Perks) with a satisfying levelling system.
* Lots of weapon options. Good starter weapons too!
* Community maps in addition to the multitude of built in ones with automatic background downloads making it all seamless.
* Skins for enemies based on events, mods and such.
* Reasonably pleasing to the eye.
* Decent enemy variety.

Bad:
* Egregious microtransactions. Even if this game was free to play I'd be insulted.
* Poor difficulty scaling
* Sticky walls leading to deaths due to being stuck on god-knows-what or simply being held in place by enemies and beaten to death without any power to stop it. This ends up being the main cause of failure (especially in solo play).
* Crawlers are dumb. They were annoying in the first game and they are still annoying now. Remove them and the game will be significantly more fun.
* Something I find annoying in multiplayer is how the game forces you to complete with your allies to get kills since money income is based on kills. This produces a non-cooperative atmosphere and is the death of many a match. Also causes me to burn out on multiplayer after a few matches. Equal money reward for all survivors would be an exceptional improvement.

KF2, albeit still in dev after its EA release back in April, is a really solid shooting co-op horror game. This installment does everything the first one did but just better: enhanced graphics, reviewed gameplay mechanics, even sexier dosh piles! It is very common for people hesitating to buy this game to wonder about its current early access state, and here is how I would ease you into buying it: The game doesn't really feel like it's in a beta, there are close to no bugs, the current content, judged at the moment minimal, will still take you on a 300h cruise and regular fixes plus dev posts makes you know this is going somewhere good.

The game makes you choose between 6 classes (at this time of writing, as there will be 10 in final release):
-Field Medic
-Berzerker
-Commando
-Support
-Firebug
-Demolitionist

Each of those have their know-hows and will require you to adapt to specific ways of playing the game, which diversifies it quite a lot. There are currently 6 very well-made official maps taking place in different post-apocaliptic settings, and 4 difficulties ranging from Normal to Hell On earth with a well-through design (the higher the difficulty, the quicker mobs get to you, rather than being even bigger HP sacks). I highly recommend this game to any co-op gamers out there!
